Diego M: quick hit: we've been seeing uneven cold-start wins across instances when using contract-cache. wondering if we should make "index-first" the default on low-memory flavors. cc @Maya P
Priya S: context: contract-cache gives big p95 wins for small-to-medium models but eats RAM on high-concurrency staging. index-first has steadier memory but slower p50.
Hannah C: is the runtime able to prioritize which tensors to contract? last trial contracted entire checkpoint and that was brutal.
Maya P: good point. we should support selective contract plans based on a manifest priority field. e.g., contract only attention query/key/value + output projections, stream others.
Diego M: that helps. operationally we need a signal in the manifest that says "streamable": true|false and a separate weight-importance score 0..100.
Priya S: propose fields: streamable, importance, preferred_contracts (list). importance used by warmup. preferred_contracts is ordered fallbacks.
Hannah C: sample manifest snippet (json):
```json
{"shard_id":"s000","slices":[{"name":"attn_q","offset":0,"len":123456,"streamable":false,"importance":95,"preferred_contracts":["dequant-8->fp16","fuse-linear-affine"]}]}
```
Diego M: love it. how should loader indicate partial-contract support? sometimes a slice can be partially streamed while contracting the head.
Maya P: loader API: stream_slice(slice_desc, mode="auto"|"stream"|"contract"). auto chooses based on memory caps and priority. returns an iterator of frames, each frame meta contains "contracted":bool and checksum.
Priya S: need to ensure checksums for concatenated frames are deterministic. suggest per-frame checksum + overall aggregate_checksum in the slice descriptor.
Hannah C: what about fallback speed? if a contract fails, runtime should be able to fall back to an inline decode path without re-fetching from origin. can loader offer a 'raw_frame_decoder' callback that consumes raw bytes and yields decoded frames?
Diego M: yes, that'd avoid extra IO. loader could expose stream_slice_raw(slice_desc) and stream_slice_decoded(slice_desc) endpoints. decoded will try contract cache first, then raw decoder.
Maya P: ops + telemetry: every decode/contract must emit tags: model, shard_id, slice_name, attempt (0=cache,1=raw,2=decoder), mem_peak, cpu_ms, duration_ms, failure_reason. Optimize needs these to recommend policies.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: loader-canary v0.7 deployed to staging-rt at 2026-03-04 11:02 UTC
Priya S: billing note: contract CPU work should be accounted differently for shared pools. we need a per-tenant token charge for contract-ms to avoid noisy-neighbor.
Hannah C: WarmupScheduler changes: accept importance threshold and dynamic calculator that demotes importance under load. Also a per-instance memory cap for concurrent contracted buffers.
Diego M: runtime policy thought: prefer streaming on nodes with < X GiB free, otherwise contract if importance >= Y. X and Y should be feature flags to iterate.
Maya P: implementation checklist I'll put in a PR: 1) manifest schema additions (streamable, importance, preferred_contracts, aggregate_checksum) 2) loader endpoints (stream_raw, stream_decoded, request_contract) 3) per-frame checksum + aggregate checksum semantics 4) telemetry tags + events 5) WarmupScheduler priority demotion + memory caps 6) accounting for contract CPU tokens.
Priya S: I'll scope a small e2e experiment: Llama-7B-ish checkpoint, 4 instance sizes, run cold-start matrix with and without selective contracts.
Hannah C: I'll add unit tests for checksum invariants and a fuzz harness for frame ordering.
Diego M: small UX: make sure error messages are actionable e.g., "contract-failed: OOM during fuse-linear on attn_q; fell back to stream-decoded" so SREs can triage quickly.
Maya P: noted. I'll draft short doc for ops and default flags. aiming to land fixture patch next week.
Priya S: FYI: observed a 18% p95 improvement on canary when contracting only top-4 importance tensors for a chat workload. will put numbers in PR.
infra-bot: incident-bot: staged OOM spike on staging-rt-03 at 3324509955 during parallel contracts; mitigation applied: lowered concurrent_contracts to 2. tagging @Priya S
Diego M: ok folks, next sync about this on Tuesday. thanks. :thumbsup:
